meta.cite: Barton O. Oliver's mTOR Atlas (live data, not an archived version; give corpus_snapshot and source_commit). doi:10.5281/zenodo.22059963

data.mechanism: In this model LARS acts as a GAP for RagD, doing for the RagC/D half what FLCN does - an alternative route from leucine to the Rags.
data.mechanism_beginner: In that model, this enzyme flips the other Rag protein into its working shape – an alternative route from leucine to the Rags.
data.boundary: Human cell biochemistry only, and cell-type dependence was never mapped. The reaction it claims - GAP activity on the RagC/D half - is the same reaction this Atlas assigns to FLCN, and the two assignments have never been reconciled head-to-head. Read together with LEU-LARS: if the upstream leucine-sensing claim does not hold, this edge loses its input.

conflict.basis: HAN2012 assigns GAP activity on RagC/D to LARS. The Atlas assigns the same reaction to FLCN, and the two assignments have not been reconciled head-to-head.
